The threshold is request-scoped, and so is opentine's application of it: 'Prompts with more than 272K input tokens are priced at 2x input and cache rates and 1.5x output for the full request.' OpenAI publishes a single 'cache writes' price ($12.50/MTok), carded on both the 5m and 1h write dimensions. 'Batch and Flex are priced at 50% of Standard rates. Fast mode is priced at 2x the applicable rates.' Ultrafast (available from 2026-09-29) is published at 6x ($60/$6/$75/$300). 'Priority processing was renamed Fast mode on July 30, 2026' and 'requests tagged priority will automatically use Fast mode', so priority is carded as the same 2x tier.

OpenAI publishes no availability date for this model; effective_from is the catalog verification date, so earlier runs report cost=unknown rather than an unverified price. No Batch, Flex, Fast or Priority price is published for this model (the pricing page's tier tables carry no gpt-5.6-cyber row), so no service modifier is carded and a tiered request stays visibly unknown rather than borrowing a sibling's rate.

The whole GPT-6.1 series is this one model. 'Cached input tokens are priced at 5% of the uncached input token rate.' OpenAI publishes one cache-write price, carded on both write dimensions. 'Fast mode prices are 2x Standard. Batch and Flex prices are 50% lower than Standard. Ultrafast mode prices are 6x Standard.' Ultrafast became available on 2026-10-08. 'Priority processing was renamed Fast mode on July 30, 2026' and 'requests tagged priority will automatically use Fast mode', so priority is carded as the same 2x tier.

cache_read is the published literal $0.25/MTok, not a family-rule derivation: the pricing page footnotes 'Cache hits and refreshes on Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 are priced at 0.025x the base input price. All other models use the standard 0.1x multiplier.' Every opentine card states cache_read outright and nothing in the engine derives it from input, so the model-specific rate cannot be overwritten by the family rule. No 'fast' modifier: fast mode is for Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Opus 5 and Claude Opus 4.8 only, so a fast-tier request on this card stays visibly unknown rather than borrowing another model's 2x. No context threshold: 'Claude 4.6 and later models ... include the full 1M token context window at standard pricing.' batch_us is the documented composition of the 0.5 Batch discount with the 1.1x US data-residency multiplier, which the page states stack.
Fast mode: 'Claude Opus 5 / Claude Opus 4.8 | $10 / MTok | $50 / MTok', exactly 2x.
Anthropic made the $2/$10 launch price permanent; the scheduled 2026-09-01 rise to $3/$15 was cancelled, so the previously catalogued standard card was removed before it could take effect.

Launch price. On 2026-10-07 Anthropic 'lowered the price of prompt cache reads on Claude Sonnet 5.5 from $0.20 USD to $0.10 USD per million tokens ... Cache writes and all other prices are unchanged', so this card closes at 2026-10-06. No fast mode.
cache_read is the published literal $0.10/MTok (0.05x base input, footnote 2). Batch $1/$5. No fast mode.

Two published price rows: prompts up to 100,000 tokens and prompts over 100,000 tokens ($0.50/$0.625/$1/$0.05/$2.50, exactly 5x every dimension). 'A request's prompt length counts all of its input tokens, including cache reads and cache writes', which is the engine's input_total, and the higher tier applies to the whole request. Batch rows are 0.5x in both tiers.

Limited availability (verified organizations only), publicly priced: 'Cache hits and refreshes on Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 are priced at 0.025x the base input price.' Batch $5/$25. No fast mode.

Priced and active but previously uncarded. Batch $1.50/$7.50; inference_geo 'us' applies 1.1x 'for Claude 4.6 and later models'.

Cache Write became a separate billing item in September 2026 (TTL 5min $3.00, TTL 1h $6.00) and the API reports it as prompt_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens. The 5-minute write equals the input price it was previously billed at, so carding it from the start of the card is cost-neutral. Chat Completions does not echo the TTL, so writes are read as 5-minute writes; a caller that opts into the 1h TTL is under-billed by $3/MTok on those writes.
'kimi-k2.5 was officially discontinued on August 31, 2026'; calls now return 404.

Requests between 00:00 and 16:00 UTC on 2026-08-16 were still billed at this flat rate but fall outside the day-granular window.

Base rates are the off-peak price; the peak window carries the 2x price. Peak/off-peak began at 16:00 UTC on 2026-08-16, so requests between 00:00 and 16:00 UTC that day were still billed flat and fall outside this day-granular window. Peak applied every day of the week until the weekend rule below.

From 00:00 Beijing time on 2026-08-23 (16:00 UTC on 2026-08-22) off-peak applies all day on Beijing-time weekends, which the pricing page states as peak 'Monday through Friday'. Every peak-eligible hour (01:00-10:00 UTC) is 09:00-18:00 the same calendar day in Beijing time, so scoping the window to UTC weekdays is exactly equivalent to the published Beijing-time rule. The rule took effect after 2026-08-22's peak windows had already passed, so the day-granular split at 2026-08-23 loses no hour. Peak hours exclude Chinese public holidays; the card is split at the 2026 weekday holidays from 2026-09-25 on.

'The legacy names deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are still accepted, but the corresponding models have been retired, their requests are served by the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model and billed at the Flash price.' deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner were discontinued on 2026-07-24 and are not aliased. 'Peak hours are 01:00 - 04:00 and 06:00 - 10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday, excluding Chinese public holidays. All other hours are off-peak, including weekends and Chinese public holidays in full.' Every peak hour is 09:00-18:00 the same calendar day in Beijing time, so splitting cards at UTC dates around the State Council's 2026 weekday holidays (09-25; 10-01, 10-02, 10-05, 10-06, 10-07) is exact. The open-ended card must be split again for the next weekday holiday once the 2027 calendar is published.

Model Studio international (Singapore, dashscope-intl) USD list price: input $0.5, output $3, Input(Implicit Cache) $0.1, Explicit Cache Creation $0.625, Explicit Cache Read $0.05 per 1M tokens. Neither vendor page publishes an availability date for this model, so the card is effective from the day its price was confirmed rather than backdated; runs before it stay unpriced. The model had no hosted price until this card and was previously held.
